source: Transcribed from the FAMILY CHORE CHART (colored-dot rotation grid).
keyFinding: The printed chart shows seven week columns, but it is really a 3-week rotation displayed 2⅓ times. Every row cycles Finley → Maryn → Arthur; rows differ only in where they start. WK7 is identical to WK1. The app should COMPUTE assignments from the formula below rather than storing a 7-column grid — that way the rotation runs forever instead of expiring after seven weeks.
formula: assignee(chore, weekIndex) = cycle[(chore.offset + weekIndex) mod 3], where weekIndex is 0-based from rotationEpoch.

rotationEpoch.note: REQUIRED BEFORE BUILD. Set this to the Sunday that WK1 began. Without it the app cannot know which week the household is currently on. The photographed chart has a hand-drawn arrow over WK2, so at photo time the family was in week 2.

verification.note: Formula reproduces all 42 printed cells exactly. Spot-check against the photo before trusting it.

relationshipToWeeklyChoreCharts.finding: This resolves the open question about the 'Weekly Chore' placeholder. Each child's personal WEEKLY CHORES chart has a 'Weekly Chore' slot on Sunday and Saturday. This rotation grid is what fills that slot.
relationshipToWeeklyChoreCharts.implication: Do NOT make 'Weekly Chore' a free-text field an adult types in each week. Resolve it automatically: look up the current rotation week, find every chore assigned to that child, and render it in their Sunday/Saturday slot with the real label. Zero weekly maintenance for the adults, which is most of the value of digitizing this.
relationshipToWeeklyChoreCharts.confirmNeeded: Each child draws 2 of the 6 rotation chores per week. Their chart shows 'Weekly Chore' in exactly 2 slots (Sunday and Saturday). That lines up perfectly — confirm it's intentional and not a coincidence.
